written: 2026-11-26, before scripts/research_v4d.py produced any number on real data
status: Fixed. Not edited after results exist. Hindsight comparison; not part of the ledger; not a forecast.
asked_for: The owner asked for the AFMX score to be scored against the most widely used indicators, to find where it falls short.
afmx: v3_long from round 1: rules/v3.json thresholds on the long series, score lifted to the floor of the indicated state. No fitting here.

benchmarks.vix_term: VIX divided by 3-month VIX (FRED VIXCLS / VXVCLS), from 2007-12
benchmarks.nfci: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index, weekly, used 5 trading days late (FRED NFCI)
benchmarks.anfci: Chicago Fed Adjusted NFCI, weekly, 5 trading days late (FRED ANFCI)
benchmarks.stlfsi: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index, weekly, 5 trading days late (FRED STLFSI4)
benchmarks.kcfsi: Kansas City Fed Financial Stress Index, monthly, used from 10 trading days after month end (FRED KCFSI)
benchmarks.ofr_fsi: Office of Financial Research Financial Stress Index, daily, 2 trading days late (financialresearch.gov)
benchmarks.ciss_us: ECB Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress for the United States, 1 trading day late (ECB Data Portal)
benchmarks.credit_spread: Moody's Baa yield minus 10-year Treasury, daily (FRED BAA10Y)
benchmarks.yield_curve: 10-year minus 3-month Treasury, sign flipped so higher = more inverted (FRED T10Y3M)
benchmarks.drawdown: Market's fall from its 252-day high (French daily market return)
benchmarks.below_200dma: Market's distance below its 200-day average, higher = further below

not_testable: CNN Fear & Greed (no official history file), MOVE and SKEW (no free primary-source history). They are compared on published facts only, not on numbers.
revision_caveat: NFCI, ANFCI, STLFSI, KCFSI and CISS are re-estimated; today's history is what is downloaded, so their numbers here are flattered. Real-time vintages are not used.
sample: Test period only, 2007-01-03 on (AFMX thresholds and nothing else were set with knowledge of earlier years). Ranking uses the days on which every available indicator has a value. 1990-2006 is reported for information.

measures.M1: AUROC for: market closes 10% or more below today's close within 63 trading days
measures.M2: AUROC for: 5% or more within 21 trading days
measures.M3: Early warning: M1 computed only on days when the market is within 5% of its 252-day high
measures.M4: Spearman correlation between the indicator and the size of the worst fall over the next 63 trading days
measures.M5: Share of the indicator's lowest-third days that were followed by the 10% fall (lower is better)
measures.M6: Share of the indicator's highest-fifth days that were followed by the 10% fall (higher is better)
measures.M7: Times per year the indicator crosses its own 80th percentile (lower is calmer). Reported, not ranked: weekly and monthly series move less by construction.

scoring: On each of M1 to M6 an indicator gets 100 x (number of indicators it beats or ties) / (number of other indicators). Overall = plain average of the six. Thirds, fifths and the 80th percentile are taken within the ranking sample for every indicator alike.
uncertainty: Moving-block bootstrap, 63-day blocks, 2,000 draws, seed 20261126. For M1 and M3, the 90% interval of (indicator minus AFMX).
what_counts_as_a_shortfall: AFMX is called behind an indicator on M1 or M3 only when the 90% interval of the difference lies above zero. A lower rank without that is reported as 'not distinguishable'. Also reported: Spearman correlation of AFMX with each indicator (how much AFMX repeats what is already free).
what_can_come_out: A scorecard and a list of shortfalls. No rule change. Any change to the rule would be a separate pre-registered test and the owner's decision.
